title: Raspberry Pi IoT Project
subtitle: Building an end-to-end sensor dashboard project

content.text: This lesson ties everything together: a Raspberry Pi reads sensors, publishes via MQTT, and a simple web dashboard shows live data.

content.code:
# Full stack: sensor → MQTT → InfluxDB → Grafana
# 1. Read sensors (DHT22 for temp/humidity)
from gpiozero import PWMLED
from adafruit_dht import DHT22
import board, paho.mqtt.client as mqtt, json, time

sensor = DHT22(board.D4)
client = mqtt.Client()
client.connect("localhost", 1883)

while True:
    try:
        temp = sensor.temperature
        hum  = sensor.humidity
        payload = json.dumps({"temp": temp, "humidity": hum, "timestamp": time.time()})
        client.publish("home/sensors/dht22", payload, qos=1)
    except RuntimeError:
        pass  # DHT occasionally misreads
    time.sleep(10)

# Install stack
sudo apt install mosquitto mosquitto-clients influxdb grafana
sudo systemctl enable --now mosquitto influxdb grafana-server

# Telegraf reads MQTT and writes to InfluxDB
# Grafana dashboard reads from InfluxDB

content.text: Use Docker Compose to run the full stack (Mosquitto, Telegraf, InfluxDB, Grafana) on a Pi 4 for a clean IoT platform.

questions.question: What role does Grafana play in this IoT stack?
questions.explanation: Grafana queries InfluxDB and renders live charts and dashboards for the sensor data.

faq.q: Can a Raspberry Pi Zero W run this stack?
faq.a: The Zero W (1 core, 512 MB RAM) can handle the Python sensor publisher and Mosquitto broker. InfluxDB + Grafana need a Pi 3 or 4.
